query: Do online sellers need to display a BIR Registration Seal Badge on their shop profiles or websites?
answer:
Yes. Online sellers and other taxpayers with an online presence are required to display the BIR Registration Seal Badge on their website, online store or platform, mobile application, social media business page, or e-commerce seller profile — in lieu of posting a copy of the BIR COR/eCOR [4].

Only the BIR Registration Seal Badge should be posted on the taxpayer's official website, mobile application, online shop, or e-commerce platform profile page [1]. Taxpayers are not required to upload their entire registration document or the full page where the badge appears; they may crop, scan, or extract only the badge image for posting [1].

rag.answer:
Ang mga benta sa isang registered export enterprise ay kwalipikado lamang sa VAT zero-rating kung ang mga ito ay **direkta at eksklusibong ginagamit sa registered project o activity** ng nasabing export enterprise [1][2][4].

Bukod dito, may mga sumusunod na kondisyon:

- Hindi kasama ang mga gastos na natamo **bago pa ang registration** ng proyekto o aktibidad sa IPA [1].
- Kailangan ng **endorsement mula sa concerned IPA**, bukod pa sa mga documentary requirements ng BIR [4].
- Kailangan ding makakuha ng **prior approval mula sa BIR** ang mga local supplier [5].
- Nalalapat lamang ito sa loob ng **maximum na 17 taon mula sa petsa ng registration**, maliban kung palawigin pa sa ilalim ng Strategic Investment Priority Plan [2].

Hindi rin kasama sa VAT zero-rating ang mga **Domestic Market Enterprises (DMEs)** [1].

query: Paano tinitiyak ang tax neutrality sa pagbili o pag-isyu ng mga Islamic bonds o Sukuk?

retrieved.label: [1] RMC No. 81-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
retrieved.text:
REVENUE MEMORANDUM CIRCULAR NO. 81-2024 issued on July 18, 2024 provides 
the tax treatment of Sukuk (Islamic Bond) as Islamic banking arrangement pursuant to the Tax 
Neutrality Provision of Republic Act No. 11439 (An Act Providing for the Regulation and 
Organization of Islamic Banks) as implemented by Revenue Regulations No. 17-2020. 
 
Sukuk issued, structured in a Shari'ah-compliant manner, but with economic characteristics 
similar to bonds, are subject to the taxes per the Circular.  The gain or profit in Sukuk is 
determined based on the specific structure and terms of the Sukuk issuance. It can be calculated 
through profit -sharing ratios, rental income, mark -up or price differentials, or the sale of

retrieved.label: [2] RMC No. 81-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
retrieved.text:
exempt from VAT. 
 
Any disposal or lease of the underlying asset, and execution of any additional instrument 
required in a Sukuk transaction, for the purpose of compliance with Shari'ah principles but 
which will not be required in a conventional bond transaction, shall be deemed excluded for 
taxation purposes. 
 
A Documentary Stamp Tax (DST) is imposed on all Sukuk instruments under Sections 176 and 
179 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, (Tax Code) unless excepted 
under Section 199(g) of the same code. 
 
Guidelines and examples of some Sukuk structures that may be encountered in practice are 
provided in the Circular.

Gains or profits realized by Sukuk holders, from Sukuk transactions, who are non-resident aliens 
not engaged in trade or business in the Philippines and non -resident foreign corporation are 
subject to twenty-five percent (25%) FWT. 
 
The Sukuk issuer is required to withhold the tax at every payment of gains or  profits and for 
purchases of asset either directly from a supplier or through an agent. 
 
Gains or profits realized by Originator/Obligor, Arranger, Manager, and Underwriter from 
Sukuk transactions are subject to regular Income Tax and Value -Added Tax (VAT ) or 
Percentage Tax, whichever is applicable. 
 
Gains or profits realized by the Special Purpose Vehicle are subject to regular Income Tax but 
exempt from VAT.

Gains or profits realized by Sukuk holders from Sukuk transactions with maturity of less than

maturity of five years or more are excluded from the gross income and are therefore exempt

Sa ilalim ng circular na ito, ang anumang pag-dispose o pag-lease ng underlying asset, at ang pag-execute ng anumang karagdagang instrumento na kailangan sa isang Sukuk transaction para sa pagsunod sa Shari'ah principles — pero hindi naman kailangan sa isang conventional bond transaction — ay itinuturing na **excluded sa taxation purposes** [2]. Bukod dito, ang isang Non-Stock, Non-Profit Educational Institution na hindi saklaw ng Section 3 ng nasabing Regulations ay sasailalim din sa 25% regular corporate income tax rate — ngunit limitado lamang ito sa bahagi ng kanilang revenues o assets na hindi aktwal, direkta, at eksklusibong ginagamit para sa educational purposes [1][4].

rag.answer:
Oo, nagkakaltas ng withholding tax ang mga e-marketplace operator sa mga ibinabayad sa kanilang online sellers.

Ayon sa RR No. 16-2023, nagpapataw ito ng withholding tax sa gross remittances ng mga e-marketplace operator at digital financial services providers sa mga sellers/merchants para sa mga kalakal o serbisyong ibinenta/binayaran sa kanilang platform [3]. Ang rate ay **1%** batay sa **one-half (1/2) ng gross remittances** [5].

Gayunpaman, hindi ito applicable kung:
- Ang annual total gross remittances sa seller/merchant sa nakaraang taxable year ay hindi lumampas sa **₱500,000.00**; o
- Ang cumulative gross remittances sa isang taxable year ay hindi pa lumampas sa **₱500,000.00** [5].

Kung ang e-marketplace platform ang tumatanggap o nangongolekta ng bayad at nagre-remit nito sa seller, dapat ibawas ang withholding tax bago ang remittance [1].

For donations consisting purely of cash, the Donor's Tax return must be filed electronically, and the tax paid either manually through an Authorized Agent Bank or electronically through the BIR's ePayment channels [1].

  - Valid government-issued IDs (or Secretary's Certificate/Board Resolution for non-individuals)
  - TIN of Donor and Donee
- An **eCAR is not required** for donations consisting exclusively of cash [3].

rag.answer:
**Ang mga donasyon na binubuo lamang ng purong cash ay may sariling panuntunan sa pag-file, pagbabayad, at mga dokumentong kailangan, ayon sa RMC No. 10-2026.**

- Saklaw nito ang mga donasyong purong cash na ginawa sa loob ng parehong calendar year, sa natural o juridical persons, kabilang ang mga organisasyon, foundation, at institusyon [1].
- Ang Donor's Tax return ay kailangang i-file **electronically** sa alinman sa available na electronic platforms (eBIRForms Facility, eFPS, o filing applications ng mga ATSP) [1].
- Ang Donor's Tax na dapat bayaran ay maaaring bayaran **manually** sa anumang Authorized Agent Bank (AAB) o **electronically** sa mga ePayment channel ng BIR [2].
- Ang mga dokumento ay isusumite sa loob ng **30 araw** mula sa petsa ng donasyon sa RDO na may hurisdiksyon sa tirahan ng Donor (indibidwal) o kung saan rehistrado ang Donor (non-individual); para sa large taxpayers, sa LT Division kung saan rehistrado ang Donor [2].

Hindi na kailangan ang eCAR para sa mga donasyong purong cash [3].

rag.answer:
Ang **Republic Act No. 12120**, na kilala rin bilang **"Philippine Natural Gas Industry Development Act,"** ang nagtatakda ng fiscal incentives para sa sektor ng natural gas **[2][4]**.

Sa ilalim ng Seksyon 38 nito, kabilang sa mga insentibo ang **exemption mula sa Value-Added Tax (VAT)** sa pagbili at pagbebenta ng **indigenous natural gas, aggregated gas,** at **power na ginawa ng generation facilities gamit ang indigenous natural gas at aggregated gas**. Ang exemption sa VAT para sa aggregated gas ay limitado lamang sa halaga ng indigenous natural gas na nabibilang dito **[1][5]**.

Bukod pa rito, ang lahat ng **Philippine Downstream Natural Gas Industry Facilities**, kapag sertipikado ng **Department of Energy**, ay sasailalim sa evaluation para sa posibleng pagkakaroon ng entitlements sa ilalim ng Strategic Investment Priority Plan, alinsunod sa mga probisyon ng NIRC **[2]**.

- Hindi pa lumalampas sa **₱500,000.00** ang cumulative gross remittances sa seller sa loob ng taxable year [2].

REVENUE MEMORANDUM CIRCULAR NO. 81-2024 issued on July 18, 2024 provides 
the tax treatment of Sukuk (Islamic Bond) as Islamic banking arrangement pursuant to the Tax 
Neutrality Provision of Republic Act No. 11439 (An Act Providing for the Regulation and 
Organization of Islamic Banks) as implemented by Revenue Regulations No. 17-2020. 
 
Sukuk issued, structured in a Shari'ah-compliant manner, but with economic characteristics 
similar to bonds, are subject to the taxes per the Circular.  The gain or profit in Sukuk is 
determined based on the specific structure and terms of the Sukuk issuance. It can be calculated

required in a Sukuk transaction, for the purpose of compliance with Shari'ah principles but 
which will not be required in a conventional bond transaction, shall be deemed excluded for 
taxation purposes. 
 
A Documentary Stamp Tax (DST) is imposed on all Sukuk instruments under Sections 176 and 
179 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, (Tax Code) unless excepted 
under Section 199(g) of the same code.

Ang tax neutrality para sa Sukuk ay tinitiyak sa pamamagitan ng **Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 81-2024** na naglalapat ng Tax Neutrality Provision ng RA No. 11439, kung saan:

- Ang anumang disposisyon o pag-upa ng underlying asset, at pag-execute ng karagdagang instrumento na kinakailangan lamang para sumunod sa Shari'ah pero hindi naman kailangan sa conventional bond, ay **hindi ipapataw ng buwis** (deemed excluded for taxation purposes) [2].
- May DST pa ring ipinapataw sa lahat ng Sukuk instruments batay sa Sections 176 at 179 ng Tax Code maliban kung saklaw ng exception sa Section 199(g) [2].

Kaya kahit may mga dagdag na transaksyong hatid ng Shari'ah-compliance, hindi sila binubuwisan para maging kapantay ng conventional bonds [1][2].

Yes — digital services are subject to VAT in the Philippines. "Digital service" covers any service supplied over the internet or other electronic network using information technology where the supply is essentially automated, and this includes online platforms, online media and advertising, cloud services, online marketplaces, online search engines, and digital goods [1].

For donations consisting purely of cash, the Donor's Tax return must be filed electronically, and the tax paid either manually through an Authorized Agent Bank or electronically through the BIR's ePayment channels [1].

Key rules under RMC No. 10-2026 [1][2][3]:
- **Coverage:** Donations of pure cash made during the same calendar year to natural or juridical persons, including organizations, foundations, and institutions [1].
- **Filing:** Electronically via eBIRForms, eFPS, or ATSP filing applications/solutions [1].
- **Documentary requirements** (submitted within **30 days** after the gift is made or completed, to the RDO having jurisdiction over the donor's residence/registration, or the LT Division for large taxpayers): notarized Deed of Donation; proof of cash transfer; proof of filing of BIR Form No. 1800; proof of payment (if applicable); Certificate of Donation (for tax-exempt donee); valid government-issued IDs (or Secretary's Certificate/Board Resolution for non-individuals); and TIN of donor and donee [2][3].

Yes — a seller may claim an output VAT credit on uncollected receivables under Section 110(D) of the Tax Code, but only for sales on account that transpired upon the effectivity of RR No. 3-2024 [2]. Availing of this benefit is merely an option, not automatic [5].

REVENUE MEMORANDUM CIRCULAR NO. 81-2024 issued on July 18, 2024 provides 
the tax treatment of Sukuk (Islamic Bond) as Islamic banking arrangement pursuant to the Tax 
Neutrality Provision of Republic Act No. 11439 (An Act Providing for the Regulation and 
Organization of Islamic Banks) as implemented by Revenue Regulations No. 17-2020. 
 
Sukuk issued, structured in a Shari'ah-compliant manner, but with economic characteristics 
similar to bonds, are subject to the taxes per the Circular.  The gain or profit in Sukuk is 
determined based on the specific structure and terms of the Sukuk issuance. It can be calculated 
through profit -sharing ratios, rental income, mark -up or price differentials, or the sale of

retrieved.label: [2] RMC No. 81-2024 Digest, p.1 (2024)
retrieved.text:
exempt from VAT. 
 
Any disposal or lease of the underlying asset, and execution of any additional instrument 
required in a Sukuk transaction, for the purpose of compliance with Shari'ah principles but 
which will not be required in a conventional bond transaction, shall be deemed excluded for 
taxation purposes. 
 
A Documentary Stamp Tax (DST) is imposed on all Sukuk instruments under Sections 176 and 
179 of the National Internal Revenue Code of 1997, as amended, (Tax Code) unless excepted 
under Section 199(g) of the same code. 
 
Guidelines and examples of some Sukuk structures that may be encountered in practice are 
provided in the Circular.

purchases of asset either directly from a supplier or through an agent. 
 
Gains or profits realized by Originator/Obligor, Arranger, Manager, and Underwriter from

Ang tax neutrality para sa Sukuk ay tinitiyak sa pamamagitan ng Tax Neutrality Provision ng RA No. 11439, na ipinatutupad ng RR No. 17-2020 [1]. Sa ilalim nito:

- Ang anumang disposisyon o lease ng underlying asset, at ang pag-execute ng karagdagang instrumento na kailangan lamang para sumunod sa Shari'ah pero hindi kinakailangan sa conventional bond, ay **hindi binubuwisan** [2].

Hindi tinatalakay ng mga dokumentong ito ang iba pang partikular na mekanismo ng tax neutrality lampas dito.
